meta.cost_model: cost(check at round t) = a + b*prefix_len(t) + c*n_flagged(t)
meta.prefix_len: t (INTERCEPT convention: a check at round t sees rounds 1..t and acts before beliefs absorb round t -- what the S1 engine does)
meta.n_flagged: size of the standing alarm list after the check (cumulative pruned senders), read off prune_events
meta.panel_size_note: Study 1 fixes the panel at N=32 agents, so the reviewer's 5-vs-32 axis is absorbed into a and is not sweepable inside S1; it is answered in alarm_burden, which spans panels of 5,7,10,15,21 and 32 agents

budget_envelopes.uniform: K_B = a*B + b*sum(uniform_B check rounds) + c*B*F_bar -- the cost the paper's own uniform-B schedule consumes at the average alarm load
budget_envelopes.early: K_B = B*(a + 2b + c*F_bar) -- B cheapest-possible (round-2) checks; the stress test, under which every later look costs strictly more than one nominal unit

meta.both_anchors_reduce_to: K_B == B under the unit model (a,b,c)=(1,0,0)

affordability_rules.plan: flags priced at F_bar -- no per-trial clairvoyance (primary)
affordability_rules.realized: flags priced at that trial's actual alarm list (reference)

meta.policy_under_cost: each policy is given the largest nominal budget in (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) whose cost fits the envelope; 0 means it cannot afford a single check and the run is unchecked

unit.note: paper's model: cost=1 per check regardless of prefix or alarm list

headline_arm_costs.note: mean over the 12 windowed cells; realized-flag pricing

mild.note: prefix term is ~20% of a check's cost at the mid-horizon (t=8)
